purpose: Make OS/browser samples joinable to retained keys instead of only class medians.
pass_condition: Every retained key has run id, sample id, helper PID, helper start/end, key timing, EventDispatch timing, and collector file names.
failure_or_expansion_trigger: Any row cannot be joined by retained key or helper process.

purpose: Test whether frequency, cluster residency, process QoS, AMP counters, or thermal/power state already separates fast and slow classes.
minimum_rows: near-key no-CPU slow; ordinary/utility fast; background/maintenance slow; fresh finite; stale finite
pass_condition: A per-sample counter state predicts the fast ordinary/utility rows and finite decay while absent from no-CPU and background/maintenance slow rows.
failure_or_expansion_trigger: Counters do not separate the fast/slow rows, or sampling cadence misses the key windows.

purpose: Discriminate Darwin scheduler/QoS placement and wakeup latency from frequency/residency explanations.
minimum_rows: same compact rows plus one repeated confirmation run
collector: `sudo trace record --plan default --add qos --add sched-processor-selection --add thread-wakeup-sampling`
pass_condition: Runnable latency, processor selection, QoS, or wakeup timing explains the class split after matching powermetrics state.
failure_or_expansion_trigger: Trace overhead changes class ordering, or trace state also fails to separate rows.

purpose: Check browser input-task queues only after OS counters do not explain the split.
minimum_rows: one no-CPU slow; one ordinary/utility fast; one background/maintenance slow; one finite fresh/stale pair
collector: CDP trace categories for scheduler/task queues, V8, runtime, and existing Gutenberg source spans
pass_condition: Browser queue/priority/task-boundary state predicts the residual after OS counters are controlled.
failure_or_expansion_trigger: Browser trace perturbs the same mechanism or duplicates an OS-counter explanation.

purpose: Change the report only when the same per-key state predicts all discriminating rows.
pass_condition: One named state variable explains no-CPU slow, ordinary/utility fast, background/maintenance slow, and finite decay rows.
failure_or_expansion_trigger: Different row families need unrelated explanations or only aggregate medians agree.
